requirement: Run an async handler over items with a fixed number of consumer tasks fed by a bounded asyncio.Queue, stop each consumer with a None sentinel, return results in input order, and raise an ExceptionGroup of every failure after all items were attempted.
skeleton: run_pipeline validating workers, a bounded queue of (index, item) jobs or None, a nested consume loop recording results and errors by index, producer puts plus one sentinel per worker, gather, then ExceptionGroup or ordered results.
caption: A worker pool built only on asyncio. run_pipeline(items, handle, workers=3, maxsize=10) raises ValueError saying workers must be at least 1 when fewer are requested. It creates an asyncio.Queue bounded by maxsize holding (index, item) tuples or None, and starts workers consumer tasks with asyncio.create_task. Each consumer loops with a walrus await on queue.get until it receives None; for every job it awaits handle and stores the result under the job index, or catches any Exception and stores it under the index instead, so one failure never stops that consumer. The producer puts every enumerated item, then puts one None per worker so each consumer exits, and awaits asyncio.gather over the tasks. If any errors were recorded it raises ExceptionGroup with the message pipeline failed and the exceptions ordered by index; otherwise it returns the results ordered by index, not by completion. The fixture asserts that items finishing out of order still come back in input order, that at most two handlers run at once with two workers and three with the default, that empty input returns an empty list and zero workers raise ValueError, and that with one worker two ValueError failures are grouped in order while the even items are still processed.

plan.intent: Process a batch of async jobs with bounded concurrency
constraints: Fewer than one worker raises ValueError
Three workers run by default and never more handlers at once than workers
Each worker stops on a None sentinel from the queue
Results follow input order regardless of completion order
Failures do not stop a worker and are raised together as an ExceptionGroup at the end

rationale.teaches: The asyncio.Queue producer and consumer pattern with one sentinel per worker, index-keyed results, and ExceptionGroup for collected failures.
rationale.why: Pool code tends to return results in completion order, drop or stop on the first failure, or miscount sentinels, and each mistake only shows up with staggered timings, a concurrency probe, or mixed failing items.

ops.docstring: Fan work out to asyncio consumers through a bounded queue closed by sentinels.

ops.stmt: from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Iterable

candidates.why_wrong: Zero workers start no consumers and the call returns an empty list instead of raising ValueError.
The default is a single worker, so default runs are serial.
Results come back in dict insertion order, which is completion order rather than input order.
Recorded errors are never raised, so failures vanish and only the successes are returned.
A consumer stops after its first failure, so later items are never processed.
